target_customer: Software teams and QA staff at web app companies that want end to end tests without writing Selenium code
problem: Writing and maintaining Selenium style end to end tests is slow and brittle, so small teams skip testing or burn engineering time on it.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription by test volume
product_category: No-code web test automation, developer tools

founders.name: Fitz Nowlan
founders.background_notes: Software engineer who worked with his co-founder at Curalate, per Technical.ly.

founders.name: Todd McNeal
founders.background_notes: First engineer then Director of Engineering at Curalate, which was later acquired by Bazaarvoice, per YC profile.

competitors.name: Mabl
competitors.what: Low code intelligent test automation for web apps
competitors.traction_then: Launched 2018 by two former Googlers; enterprise DevOps customers
competitors.funding_then: GV backed, amount not recorded here

competitors.name: Testim
competitors.what: AI assisted low code test authoring and maintenance, also native mobile

technical_complexity.rationale: Recording user flows in a cloud browser and replaying them reliably across flaky sites is standard but fiddly engineering, with infrastructure for parallel browser runs.

defensibility.rationale: Customers accumulate test suites, which adds some lock in, but rivals such as Mabl and Testim already offered similar low code tools and features could be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not kill it. SmartBear bought Reflect in January 2024 to add generative AI testing.

market_need_then: Testing was a known pain point for web teams, and Mabl and Testim had shown paid demand for low code testing by 2018 and 2019. The founders had faced the problem themselves at Curalate.

branding.domain_note: Used reflect.run, which now redirects to SmartBear's product page. Many unrelated Reflect brands exist, including a notes app and a journaling startup.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch, VentureBeat and Technical.ly for funding and launch, but the name is generic and shared by several products, and no community or merch evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: Reflect was a small team of ex Curalate engineers that raised a 1.8 million dollar seed in early 2021 from Battery and Craft and kept a lean operation of about six people. It added AI features such as natural language tests and was acquired by SmartBear in January 2024 at an undisclosed price, a capital efficient strategic exit for a well covered niche with strong competitors.
notes: Seed amount is reported by Technical.ly and CityBiz; Employbl and CB Insights give about 1.85M to 1.93M total. Seedtable lists a separate 2M pre-seed in September 2022 that could not be confirmed, so it is not recorded as a round. VentureBeat article date was not visible in the snippet, so competitor source_date is approximate. Brand name origin not found.
